title.narrative: Lifesaving Sexual and Reproductive Health Response Through Fixed and Mobile Services in Gaza

description.narrative: ltpgtDespite the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, humanitarian conditions across Gaza remain extremely fragile. Years of hostilities, mass displacement, and extensive damage to health infrastructure continue to place women and girls—particularly pregnant women, new mothers, and adolescents—at serious risk. Many families are returning to areas where primary health care facilities are partially functional or non-operational, while remaining services are overstretched and under-resourced. Although the movement of SRH commodities into Gaza has resumed through multiple corridors, shortages persist and preventable maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality remain unacceptably high. Timely, coordinated action is therefore required to restore lifesaving SRH services, address access barriers for displaced populations, and ensure continuity of essential supplies during this narrow window of improved access.ltbrgtThis project delivers an integrated SRH response aligned with Health Cluster priorities through six complementary activities combining SRH mobile and fixed-facility SRH services in partnership with three local NGOs, and strengthened SRH supply delivery by UNFPA.ltbrgtFirst, the project will reinforce fixed clinic–based SRH service delivery across the Gaza Strip through UNFPA’s partnership with Al Awda Health and Community Association (Awda). Support to seven Awda primary health care clinics will ensure the availability of specialized SRH personnel and essential support staff to provide antenatal and postnatal care, family planning, management of sexually transmitted infections, and obstetric and gynecological services, supported by clear referral pathways to secondary-level care. ltbrgtSecond, to overcome financial barriers, a targeted SRH subsidy mechanism implemented by Awda will enable displaced women, women with disabilities, and women from female-headed households to access essential diagnostics, medicines, and minor SRH-related procedures that would otherwise be unaffordable or unavailable, with utilization monitored through existing reporting systems. ltbrgtThird, to further strengthen access to fixed clinics and integrated services, UNFPA, through its local partner Juzoor for Health Social Development, will continue oPt HF-funded SRH services to women and girls—including emergency obstetric care, antenatal and postnatal care, family planning, STI prevention and treatment, and clinical management of rape—at three medical points across Gaza governorates. In parallel, Juzoor will provide integrated psychosocial and GBV-sensitive health awareness sessions in the surrounding communities.ltbrgtRecognizing that many populations remain unable to reach fixed facilities, the project will expand access through mobile outreach of SRH services implemented by UNFPA’s partner, Palestine Medical Relief Society (PMRS). Six mobile medical teams will operate across North Gaza Governorate, Gaza, Middle Area and Khan Younis, delivering basic SRH consultations, maternal health services, psychosocial support, health education, and referrals to displaced and hard-to-reach communities.ltbrgtFinally, to sustain all service delivery modalities, UNFPA will ensure the procurement and distribution of essential SRH supplies across SRH facilities in the Gaza Strip. As the pipeline agency for SRH commodities and chair of the SRH Working Group, UNFPA will coordinate allocation, monitor consumption, and address emerging gaps to ensure quality, continuity, and complementarity of services.ltbrgtTogether, these interventions will deliver immediate, lifesaving impact by restoring access to essential SRH care, reducing preventable maternal and newborn deaths, and strengthening the resilience of frontline health services at a critical and fragile moment when scale-up is needed.ltbrgtlt/pgt
